articles.question_title: What can an AI PM learn from a pilot that keeps human approval explicit?
articles.summary: The synthetic case note describes a meeting-summary pilot that kept a human approval step and source-link checks before external sharing.
articles.why_it_matters: This is a useful AI PM pattern because the workflow boundary and review owner are explicit even before a production claim is made.
articles.business_angle: Small teams can test a narrow workflow while limiting the risk of sending unreviewed summaries to external stakeholders.
articles.ai_pm_angle: The product requirement is not only summarisation quality; it also includes source attribution, approval ownership, and a measurable pilot plan.
articles.risk_note: 未確定事項：The synthetic note does not provide independent verification. No time-saving measurement or production deployment evidence is available.

articles.question_title: How should AI PMs separate a workflow demo from production evidence?
articles.summary: The synthetic demo shows a pasted source note, claim-level source links, and an explicit boundary between a workflow prototype and measured production results.
articles.why_it_matters: Timestamped evidence makes it easier to review whether a video demonstrates a workflow pattern or merely makes an outcome claim.
articles.business_angle: Teams can use a small prototype to align on review ownership before spending effort on production integration.
articles.ai_pm_angle: An AI PM should define evidence capture and evaluation boundaries as part of the product workflow, not as post-publication cleanup.
articles.risk_note: 未確定事項：The video does not provide an independent production metric. The synthetic example does not establish whether the workflow scales beyond the demo.
